Population increased in Exeter

The estimated population of Exeter in 2024 was 138,399 usual residents, a rise of 2.0% since 2023.

This meant that Exeter's rate of population change placed it among the 10 percent fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Exeter increased by 6.8%.

Over this slightly longer period, Exeter was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Exeter

The average (median) age fell to 35 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Exeter has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Exeter is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Exeter's population of 138,399 usual residents was made up of:

  • 20,042 people aged 0 to 15 years, (14.5%)
  • 95,625 people aged 16 to 64 years, (69.1%)
  • 22,732 people aged 65 years and over, (16.4%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Exeter has a higher proportion of people aged 16 to 64 years (69.1% compared with 62.8% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Exeter, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Exeter
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Exeter, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 139 people (-0.1%). In total, there were 1,083 births and 1,222 deaths in Exeter.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 871 (0.6%). There were 16,907 people entering the area and 16,036 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Exeter's population of 2,006 (1.5%) as a result of 5,227 people entering the area and 3,221 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Exeter was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Exeter in mid-2023 is 135,708.

Within this, international migration was revised downwards by 227 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 1,115 people.

Overall, there was an revision downwards of 1,342 people.
